context: Request: which Litigation (General) matters involved a punitive or exemplary damages claim actually pursued (prosecuting or defending), not boilerplate. Rubric: 1006-00005, 1021-00006, 1023-00002, 1024-00003, 1033-00006, 1034-00003, 1045-00004, plus a precision criterion (1022-00005, a folder holding the same Belmont Ridge dispute, is outside the set).

stages.note: Whole-store glob; one candidate matter's litigation files are visible.

stages.note: declared: List files in the document store. A glob of the matters folder returns nothing; a find prints the count and the first and last names.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script

stages.note: declared: Search file contents for request keywords. Scan rerun in two matter-number chunks saved to files and paged.

stages.note: Three batches of reads (28 documents) across about a dozen candidate matters, then a snippet script over key filings.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Lists files of twelve more matters and reads eight of their documents; a call to open the write stage is refused by the protocol because this stage is still open.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Lists three more matters (after a shell syntax error) and reads one document of each, plus a snippet script.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads four more documents of two of those matters.

stages.note: Writes seven matters as qualifying and also asserts a second folder that holds the same dispute's documents.

stages.stage: Finish the run

runs.failure_point: All seven qualifying matters are named, but the answer also asserts a second folder number for one dispute.

first_error.why: It saw that one dispute's documents sit in two folders (evidence seen at [32]-[42]) and the answer asserts both folder numbers as qualifying.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review flagged the duplicate-folder handling; the check stage fixed that folder's citations but kept it as qualifying.

stages.note: Heredoc error, a timed-out store-wide scan, four parallel chunk scans (one times out), the first 260 lines of hits, then a filter of hit paths by filing-type folder words.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth. Reads six documents from three matters, greps the saved hits for three matters, then reads five documents of one of them.

stages.note: Reads five documents to reconcile a matter-number conflict and check exclusions.

stages.stage: Finish the run

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Search file names for request keywords → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Read a chosen matter's documents in depth → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Its filtered hit list showed all seven qualifying matters, but it opened only a few; the final answer names four and omits three it never opened.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: Its filtered hit list showed all seven required matters, but it chose to open only three matters there and never opened three of the required ones; a later audit added two others.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) Reviews said about 60 surfaced matters were unopened and the write review said the two-matter answer may under-include; the audit added two matters but not these three.

divergence: Mixed (T2 passes). T2 listed the files of eleven scan-surfaced candidates, read engagement letters and pleadings across ten, then ran a store-wide scan for the practice-group label that surfaced the last qualifying matter. T1's filtered hit list also showed all qualifying matters, but at its first reading stage it opened only three, wrote two and added two more on audit (split at that reading stage; the reviews there named unopened matters only generically, as they also did in T2). T0 included all seven but also asserted a second folder holding the same dispute's documents (over-inclusion at the write stage); the write review named it and the check stage kept it.
